⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 45 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `97f6814cf6fe5158d5204430de53c07504d9f88c` — the merge of head `7e6f3db193e37290d890a922c478eb687ad709f5` into base `0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 97f6814cf6fe5158d5204430de53c07504d9f88c && git checkout 97f6814cf6fe5158d5204430de53c07504d9f88c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4 7e6f3db193e37290d890a922c478eb687ad709f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4 && git merge --no-ff 7e6f3db193e37290d890a922c478eb687ad709f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- One new public export, `masterDetailRequiredOmitted (function)` on `@objectstack/spec/data`: RIGHT. Both ledgers gain exactly that one row, and `data/index.ts` uses a named re-export, so the stamper `recordMasterDetailRequiredOmissions` stays off the published surface (the package `exports` map offers no deep path into `src/data`).
- Parse accept set: UNCHANGED, right. The stamp is applied after `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` succeeds; no schema, refinement or refusal moves. `required` stays the parsed `false`, so `controlledByParentMasterOf`, the security plugin, `os validate`, `os build` and the compiled artifact read the optional master exactly as ruling A has it.
- A non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable `Symbol.for('objectstack.field.masterDetailRequiredOmitted')` property on parsed fields: RIGHT as a derived surface. It is invisible to `Object.keys`, `JSON.stringify`, structured clone, spread and the strict `FieldSchema`; no source under `packages/*/src` walks symbol keys (`Reflect.ownKeys`, `getOwnPropertySymbols`: zero hits), so no data reader sees a new key.
- `os lint` accept set: NARROWS on one spelling, right and intended. A default strict `defineStack` stack whose cbp `master_detail` omits `required` on the sole master now gets `relationship/master-detail-required` at `error` (exit 1) where it got exit 0. That is the verdict ruling record 6687830530 states ("`os lint` errors on the omitted spelling") and the published entry `cbp-optional-master-admitted` already promises; explicit `false` and `true` still lint clean. `lintDataModel` has one caller (`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts`), so no publish verdict moves.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` is right: both packages are moved by the diff, and AGENTS.md ships a non-protocol change, widening included, as `patch`. `Clause-②: yes` is right (one added public export; the claim was corrected to `yes` in 6897655754 and 6897667140) and carries no arm, which is well formed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write is added, refused or re-read by the parse; the new finding is a lint verdict the entry already declared, and the changeset body states it in plain words for a project whose CI runs `os lint`. Both lines are in the PR body and the changeset, and `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions, the reader's public name: answered, A, `masterDetailRequiredOmitted` as shipped. The record is stamped only on `master_detail` fields of `controlled_by_parent` objects, and the name carries that scope; B and C would read as a general per-field fact the producer does not record.
- Deviation, `Clause-②: yes` where the claim expected `no`: accepted, correct (see ②).
- Deviation, the checklist row `cli.validate-v18-authoring-verdicts` rev 4 to 5: accepted. PR #33929 wrote "default strict door, `os lint` exit 0"; this diff makes that sentence false, so correcting it in the same PR is owed, and the claim 6897667140 names the file. The row itself is the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- Deviation, no assignee on the PR: the seat's to set; not a contract matter.
- Deviation, `check:generated` reconciled at the 6144 heap: accepted as a container limit; the CI verdict is `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, green on this head.
- Security: no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`; no `security` label is owed by this record.
- Not escalated: nothing here needs a maintainer decision. The seat's call (fix the reach, not the prose) is the reading ruling A itself gives.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Against the ruling. Record 6687830530, option A: the raw parse reads an omitted `required` as the optional master, and `os lint` errors on the omitted spelling. The first half is untouched (the value stays `false`, nothing is refused). The second half was false on the default door and is made true by the only party that holds both the authored and the parsed field, `buildDefinedStack`. This keeps #31470 / PR #31523's reading (B there: do not refuse the omission at the parse) rather than reversing it.

Tried to break the stamp on every path between `defineStack` and `lintDataModel`, reading the head tree:

- `buildDefinedStack`: `normalized` is the post-normalization authored input; the D2 conversion `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted` is `retiredFromLoadPath`, so it does not write `required` into it first. Map-form `objects` keep order through `normalizeMetadataCollection`, and the stamper also matches by `name`, so a misaligned pair is skipped, never mis-stamped. zod builds new field objects, so the author's own literals are not mutated. `Field.masterDetail()` writes no `required`, so the helper spelling is recorded too; `ObjectSchema.create()` has already forced `true`, so it is not.
- `mergeActionsIntoObjects` after the stamp: copies the object (`{ ...obj, actions }`), keeps the `fields` map and each field by reference. Holds.
- `loadConfig` spread: top level only. Holds, and it is the reason given for field-level placement; that reason is true in `packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`.
- `os lint`'s second `normalizeStackInput`: array pass-through plus copy-on-write conversions that have nothing left to convert on a parsed stack. Holds.
- `authoringRuleUnionStack`: identity, or a fold that reuses the item references. Holds.
- `composeStacks`: one stack is returned by identity; `mergeObjects` builds `fields: { ...existing.fields, ...obj.fields }`, field references kept. Holds.
- `structuredClone`, a JSON round trip, the compiled artifact, the save doors, a bare `ObjectSchema.safeParse`: the record is absent and the field reads as the explicit optional master, which is what every door read before this PR. Fails toward no new finding and no refusal; stated in the module header and pinned by a test.
- `defineStack({ strict: false })`: no stamp, the key is still absent, the rule reports it as before.
- Two copies of the package (CLI and project): `Symbol.for` reads the same key. An older project copy writes no record and gets the pre-record reading.

Declared contract or side channel. Declared: the reader is a named, ledgered export with a module header that states producer, reader, placement and fail direction; the sole consumer imports it rather than re-deriving the symbol; and the shape follows two standing precedents (`stack-provenance.ts`, `filter-subtree-provenance.ts`, both `Symbol.for`, non-enumerable). It is no consumer-side dialect in the AGENTS.md sense: the consumer is the author-time linter, the producer writes the fact, and no runtime reader tolerates anything new. Nothing else in the platform reads the parsed value differently: the reader has one call site.

Per file:

- `packages/spec/src/data/master-detail-required-omission.ts`: holds. Reader and stamper agree with the header sentence by sentence, except the nits below.
- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: holds. The call sits after a successful parse and before the later judgements, on the strict path only; the comment is exact.
- `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`: holds. Named export of the reader only; comment exact.
- `packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts`: holds. The added sentence is true, including "nothing here reads that record".
- `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts` (implementing): agrees. `optionalMaster` now needs `required === false` and no record; a stamped sole master falls into `missingRequired` and `eitherSpelling`, so message ("declares no required: write true ... or false ..."), path (`.required`) and fix are the ones the raw door already gave. A stamped second `master_detail` is judged as before (it was already reported at `false`).

Nits (no effect on correctness or on the ruled contract; prose-face fix or a follow-up card, not a head move):

- N1 (nit): `master-detail-required-omission.ts` header, "so no third party can attest an authored spelling it never saw". `Symbol.for` is the global registry, so a third party can write the key; what is true is that the stamper is not published. The only thing a forged record earns is a lint error on the forger's own field. Same wording limit as the `stack-provenance.ts` precedent.
- N2 (nit): `data-model-rules.ts` docblock, "This rule sees the omission on every stack `os lint` loads" is wider than the next sentence, which correctly excepts a field that lost the record. One case of that exception is worth a follow-up card rather than a change here: objects of an already-parsed stack fed into a second strict `defineStack` (not `composeStacks`) arrive with `required: false` written, are re-parsed into new field objects, and lose the record. No example, skill or scaffold in the tree does this, and the result is the pre-record reading; the stamper could carry the record forward by also treating a stamped authored field as omitted.

Out of the diff, read only: the same docblock's older line "a missing `required` since ruling B" predates ruling A and was not touched by this PR.
